D023-D013_h001.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—since the winter quiet settled in, really. Out at the ranger station, it’s just me most days, and the silence gets loud. I don’t know when it started, but sometimes in the evenings, after my patrol, I end up eating… a lot. More than I should. A whole package of pasta, maybe some canned meat, bread, dessert—just keep going even after I’m full. I don’t plan it, but the kitchen’s there, and the loneliness feels heavier once the sun’s down.

I’ve started eating in the back room, not the common area, just so no one sees. Not that there’s anyone around. Used to share meals with folks during shift changes, but now I wait till they leave. It’s not every day, maybe two or three times a week? But when it happens, I don’t stop till my stomach aches.

I’m not sad all the time, but some mornings I can’t find a reason to start the coffee. I sleep okay, mostly. Just… feel hollow sometimes. Not like before my wife passed, not that deep grief—but like a shadow’s moved in. I can’t tell if I’m slipping or just getting old.

    B. Binge-Eating Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
    D. Anorexia Nervosa

D023-D013_h002.question:

My wife jokes about me always bringing snacks home, but she doesn’t know it’s because I’m hiding how much I’m actually eating.

Lately, things just feel heavier, you know? I’m not as interested in doing much, even when I’m home. I sleep when I can, but it’s not restful.
